title: ECB staff macroeconomic projections for the euro area, March 2026
summary: ECB staff project euro area GDP growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.3% in 2027, and 1.4% in 2028, revised down from December 2025 estimates due to Middle East conflict impacts on energy prices. Annual headline HICP inflation is projected to rise from 2.1% in 2025 to 2.6% in 2026, with a quarterly spike to 3.1% in Q2 2026 driven by energy price surges via Strait of Hormuz disruptions, before declining to 2.0% by 2027.
key_points: GDP growth revised down 0.3pp for 2026 and 0.1pp for 2027 versus December 2025 projections; 2028 outlook unchanged at 1.4%
HICP inflation revised up 0.7pp to 2.6% for 2026, 0.2pp for 2027, and 0.1pp for 2028 versus prior projections
Baseline energy assumptions: oil prices to peak around $90/barrel and gas at €50/MWh in Q2 2026, then decline per futures
Adverse scenario assumes oil peaks at $119/barrel and gas at €87/MWh in Q2 2026, with inflation 0.9pp higher in 2026
Severe scenario assumes oil peaks at $145/barrel and gas at €106/MWh, with inflation 1.8pp higher in 2026 and 2.8pp higher in 2027
Middle East war causing shipping disruptions through Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and LNG trade
HICPX (core) inflation projected to moderate from 2.4% in 2025 to 2.1% by 2028, tempered by euro appreciation and Chinese import penetration
Euro area lost global market shares despite some tariff relief on US exports versus December 2025
why_it_matters: These ECB staff projections represent the institution's analytical baseline for economic outlook. The 0.7pp upward revision to 2026 inflation combined with downward GDP revision increases stagflation risk and complicates ECB easing decisions. Scenarios spanning oil from $90-$145/barrel illustrate tail risks from Middle East escalation that could force hawkish policy response. The document does not include monetary policy reaction functions per ECB convention for staff projections.
macro_context: The Middle East conflict has introduced significant energy price uncertainty. Baseline assumes futures-priced reduction in energy costs allows temporary growth slowdown with subsequent rebound. However, domestic demand (bolstered by resilient labor market and German infrastructure/defense spending) remains the projected growth driver over the medium term. Wage growth moderation is slower than prior projections due to inflation compensation effects. The baseline projects headline HICP at 2.6% in 2026, 2.0% in 2027, and 2.1% in 2028.

issues_found: Source URL is missing - violates archival attribution requirements

Published_at date (2026-03-11) appears to be the projection cut-off date, not the publication date - actual publication date may be later in March 2026

Source body truncated before completion of severe scenario section; 2028 inflation differential between adverse (1.6%) and severe (2.8%) scenarios noted in record but full verification against Table 1 not possible
No monetary policy guidance or rate expectations extracted from baseline projections - record focuses only on economic forecasts without connecting to policy implications

notes: Source is ECB staff working paper providing formal economic projections. Clear macro catalyst relevance. Document contains baseline projections plus two hypothetical stress scenarios (adverse and severe) illustrating uncertainty range from Middle East conflict. No monetary policy reaction functions are included in scenarios per ECB convention. Source type classified as research_paper per staff projection document nature.
